title: [News] AI Interposers Grow Larger, Raising HBM4E Cooling Challenges: How Samsung, SK hynix Are Responding
source_used: TrendForce News (fulltext from main session), relaying Chosun Biz and ETNews
key_facts: Chosun Biz: interposers, which connect compute chips and HBM, are expected to grow dramatically; Samsung is preparing technologies to handle heat in HBM4E, which it plans to start mass-producing next year.

Current AI interposers are already about 5.5 times the 858 mm² maximum area an EUV lithography system can expose in one shot; an equipment-industry official expects nine, 12 and eventually up to 40 times that area.
Cause: limits of process scaling and growing use of chiplet-based 2.5D packaging, combining several compute chiplets and HBM stacks on one interposer.

Samsung is exploring lower-power designs plus hybrid copper bonding (HCB), which replaces micro bumps between stacked DRAM dies with direct copper connections, and heat path block (HPB), which adds a thermal path around the D2D PHY in the HBM base die.
Samsung showed HCB at Nvidia's GTC 2026 in March and is validating HPB with HBM4E, planning to introduce it with HBM5.
ETNews: SK hynix's iHBM places a highly thermally conductive but electrically insulating material around the D2D PHY and expects to cut thermal resistance by about 30%.
quote_evidence: The report notes that current AI interposers are already around 5.5 times the 858 mm² maximum area that an EUV lithography system can expose in a single shot.
Samsung is currently validating the technology with HBM4E and plans to introduce it with HBM5.
The company expects the design to reduce thermal resistance by around 30%.
why_it_matters_hint: Heat limits how much memory and processing can be packed into AI chips, so cooling fixes shape how powerful future AI hardware can be; the 30% figure is SK hynix's own expectation.
event_date: 12 Oct 2026 (TrendForce relaying Chosun Biz and ETNews)
